synthesis_provenance.first_pass_synthesis_verbatim:
I’m trying to pin down what makes an AI an agent instead of just a chatbot with confidence.

Because an agent can do more than answer once. It can make decisions, choose tools, read documents, search for information, write things down, call APIs, and keep track of what it’s doing.

Which is exciting.

And also exactly how you end up with a digital intern reorganizing your entire life because you asked it to “be helpful.”

The useful question isn’t, “Is this technically an agent?”

It’s: what can it actually do when it gets access to tools, information, and a job with more than one step?

I’ve got a pile of notes, several bad ideas, and a growing suspicion that the smallest useful test is going to become a much larger problem.

Well… now I want to try it.

synthesis_provenance.corrective_pass_synthesis_verbatim:
I found my old workshop-agent notes, and I’m doing that dangerous thing where I read my own handwriting and think, “Oh. This was a smaller idea before I gave it more context.”

I’m researching AI agents again, but I’m trying not to let the word “agent” turn into fog.

An agent is not just a chatbot with a little hat on. It can make decisions, choose tools, search for information, read documents, write information, call APIs, and work through more than one step. It can keep state. It can react when something changes.

Which is where this gets interesting.

A language model can give you one very confident answer. Sometimes it’s useful. Sometimes it’s confidently wrong, which is a deeply efficient way to waste an afternoon.

But give that system tools, information, memory, and an environment? Now it can actually *do* things. Or attempt to. There is a difference, and I plan to find it.

I keep coming back to the same question: what happens when the AI has a job, access to the stuff it needs, and enough context to make choices about the project?

Could it organize the work? Could it pick the wrong objective? Could it remember something important? Could two agents cooperate—or become extremely polite obstacles in each other’s way?

I’m not calling that consciousness. I’m calling it a very suspicious pile of notes that deserves a proper test.

If you’ve got an agent experiment you think I should build, throw it at me.
